FINDINGS:

I could not run the experiment (requirement 3), so every conflict count below is predicted, not measured. The Bash tool is disabled in this session, so I couldn't run git. I wrote a ready script, `/tmp/clexp_scripts/exp.sh <CHANGELOG.md> <new-empty-dir>`. It builds five branches per variant (plain, union, append, fragment, orchestrator-writes) and merges them in three orders with `git merge --squash`. I never executed it, so it is untested. I changed no project files.

**What the primary material shows**
- **No enforcement exists.** There is no `.git` directory, `.gitattributes`, hook, CI, lint or `Makefile`. `pyproject.toml` is the only config file.
  - A case-insensitive grep for "changelog" outside `docs/tasks/` hits only `CHANGELOG.md`, `CLAUDE.md:3` (a bare link) and `app/mcp_stdio.py:1761`. The `mcp_stdio.py` hit is an unrelated docstring about Codex debate rounds.
  - No `pipelines/` prompts exist in this snapshot.
  - So the rule "every task must add an entry" is not written anywhere I can see in this snapshot. It may live in prompts or a task template that aren't here.
  - The "orchestrator merge code" is `app/workspace.py`, around lines 1256-1370. It runs `git merge-tree --write-tree` as a precheck and returns `{"ok": False, "conflicts": [...]}` on conflict. Otherwise it runs `git merge --squash <branch>`.
  - `CLAUDE.md:139` tells the orchestrator to run `check_conflict` before merging and to cherry-pick onto a fresh branch from main if there is a conflict.
- **No logs or transcripts show a CHANGELOG merge failure.** The `docs/tasks/*` files mention the changelog, but I found no conflict record. I did not read them all.
- **Insertion point.** In `CHANGELOG.md` there are 65 `## vX.Y.Z — date — #task` sections, newest first. The newest sits at line 7, directly under the header (v2.35.5 at line 7, v2.35.4 at line 22, and so on). I treat prepending a new section at line 7 as the de facto convention, inferred from the file's history. I found no instruction that says it.
- **A second shared point is the version number.** Each entry bumps the version. The file already has duplicates: v2.31.0, v2.32.0 and v2.33.0 each appear twice (lines 132-177 and 158-291). The note at lines 3-5 says this came from two parallel lines of work sharing numbers.

**Cause (from reading the file, not measured)**
Five branches cut from one commit each insert a hunk at line 7. Git sees five different insertions at the same spot. After the first merge, every later branch overlaps the hunk already in main. For plain prepend, I predict conflicts = N−1 for N branches in any merge order: N=2 gives 1, N=3 gives 2, N=4 gives 3, N=5 gives 4. The version-header lines would collide as well.

**Fixes (predicted, not measured)**

| Fix | Conflicts for N=2..5 | Agent tool calls per task | Does the rule check still pass? |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) Fragment file per branch, assembled at release | 0 (unique filenames) | 1 `Write`, about the same as now, since an agent today needs a read plus an edit | Only if the check looks for "a new file in `changes/`" instead of "a diff in `CHANGELOG.md`". No check exists today, so it needs writing. |
| (b) `merge=union` in `.gitattributes` | Not reliably 0. Union keeps both sides at textual conflicts, but the order is arbitrary. | 1 edit, unchanged | Yes, a diff in `CHANGELOG.md` still exists. |
| (c) Orchestrator writes the entry after merging | 0 | 0 for the agent. The orchestrator makes 1 edit per merge, and these are serial. | Yes at the main-branch level. A per-branch check fails and must be dropped. |

For (b), I expect it to work for N=2..5 on pure insertions, but I haven't confirmed it. Worse, it silently interleaves entries and can break the version sections. In this file that would damage the `## vX.Y.Z` structure. Also, `merge-tree` and `git merge --squash` both honour the attribute.

**Recommendation**
Use (a). Entries go in `changes/<task-id>.<type>.md`, and a release step concatenates them and assigns the version number. This also fixes the duplicate-version problem that (b) and (c) leave in place. It adds no tool calls, and the file-existence check is cheap to write. If you can't change the format, use (c) as the fallback. It has no per-agent cost, but it serialises the orchestrator and loses the "agents document their own work" habit.

**Not verified**
- All conflict counts and tool-call counts above.
- Whether any agent prompt or task template tells agents where to put the entry, or whether any enforcement of the rule exists outside this snapshot.
- Whether any real merge failed on `CHANGELOG.md`.
- The git version's `merge=union` behaviour on this file.
